text:
ana (arch): quick follow-up from the Traffic Shepherd RFC. want to settle a few interface decisions before i turn this into an RFC diff. TL;DR: central coordinator vs local agents, what signals we expose, and how fallbacks get triggered automatically.

devon (eng-runtime): +1. can we scope: this is for canary/A-B traffic only, not quota-based autoscaling, right?

ana (typo correction) ana (arch): yes just canary and staged swaps. autoscale is separate.

mike (eng-sre): question: do we still need a global decision plane for fast rollback, or can we rely on bounded local heuristics? global allows coordinated cross-region rollback but is a single point of velocity.

devon (eng-runtime): my take: keep a light-weight global coordinator that issues intents (e.g., "scale-down variant-B to 0.0 in 30s", "pause rollout"), but agents should be able to act on local hard-fail signals immediately. coordinator only drives gradual adjustments and policy.

sasha (eng-platform): important: the runtime API must be tiny. something like PATCH /rollouts/:id with a small policy blob. we can't have agents poll large models.

li (product): also add product constraints: teams want deterministic fallbacks for compliance customers. we should expose strong SLA guardrails: max-failure-rate, token-latency-threshold, and an emergency cutoff flag.

mike (eng-sre): agree. and we need clear priorities: safety overrides (e.g., emergency cutoff) > automated rollback > scheduled ramp-down.

devon (eng-runtime): propose an interface: rollout intent contains edges (primary, variant), percent, metric-guards (histogram reference keys), and actions on breach: [pause, rollback-step, emergency-route]. Agents subscribe to intents and emit signal events.

ana (arch) ana (arch): sketch of intent JSON (for clarity):
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "r-2026-03-traffic-42",
  "steps": [ { "duration_s": 3600, "target_pct": 10 }, { "duration_s": 3600, "target_pct": 30 } ],
  "guards": { "p99_latency_ms": 800, "error_rate": 0.03 },
  "on_breach": "rollback-step"
}
```

sasha (eng-platform): nice. keep guards referential to metric keys we already collect (route.p99, route.err). also add a probe-level check: probe.failure_ratio > 0.2 triggers immediate fallback.

devon (eng-runtime): one tricky bit: how do we resolve conflicting directives? e.g., global says continue, local agent sees infra OOM and wants to cut variant. we need a priority ladder and a short-circuit for safety signals.

mike (eng-sre): propose ordering: emergency safety signals (node OOM, queue-depth exceed) > operator manual action > local automated safety (local infra) > global rollout plan. emergency signals are sticky for Xs unless cleared.

li (product): for auditability, every state change needs an event with actor, reason, and traces of the relevant metric windows. retention configurable per tenant.

devon (eng-runtime): telemetry model: agents emit 1) aggregated metrics (windowed), 2) event stream for safety triggers, 3) optional heap/perf samples for debugging. keep payload small.

ana (arch) ana (arch): we should avoid coupling to metric names. rollout engine should accept logical signals (latency, error, divergence) and map them to metric keys via a per-tenant mapping.

sasha (eng-platform): refactor ask: decouple "decision engine" from "execution engine". decision engine computes new weights but execution engine handles routing changes, warmup, and kv-cache priming. makes it easier to test.

devon (eng-runtime): yes — decision engine can run in control-plane, execution sits in runtime-plane. runtime-plane must support atomic weight updates with optional grace window.

mike (eng-sre): runbook implications: provide a quick CLI to inject an emergency cutoff and to query the last N events for a rollout id. canary-bot should be able to run these safely.

canary-bot: /rollout status r-2026-03-traffic-42 -> active step 2, target_pct 30, last_event "probe.failure_ratio breached", action in progress: rollback-step by agent us-west-1.

li (product): UX: product wants a visibility panel showing active guard breaches, timeline, and who/what triggered rollback. include links to traces.

ana (arch) ana (arch): open questions we need to decide before RFC: 1) priority ladder exact ordering and what signals are considered "emergency"; 2) event schema for audit logs; 3) rollback granularity (step vs full); 4) how long agent-local decisions remain authoritative before the coordinator reconciles.

devon (eng-runtime): my proposals: 1) emergencies = infra OOM, queue depth > 5x normal, disk pressure, or probe failure_ratio>0.2; 2) event schema = minimal (ts, actor, reason, metric_snapshot, prior_state, new_state); 3) default rollback granularity = step, with operator flag to full-evict; 4) local decisions authoritative for 30s unless overridden by operator.

mike (eng-sre): 30s seems reasonable for fast fail; might need to tune. add a guard: coordinator can declare agent stale if it misses heartbeats > 15s.

sasha (eng-platform): implementation note: build decision engine as a separate K8s service (stateless) that computes intents and writes to a compact intent store (etcd). agents watch intents via long-poll. avoids heavy RPCs.

ana (arch) ana (arch): ok i'll draft the RFC diff with these suggestions. devon/sasha/mike/li please comment on the draft when i post. short ask: if you have strong objections to the ordering or timing, flag now. otherwise i'll aim to merge next Wed. :thumbsup:

devon (eng-runtime): no blockers from me. will open a small PR for the runtime client API.

mike (eng-sre): +1. i'll prototype the CLI hooks for emergency cutoffs.

sasha (eng-platform): +1. will add intent store sketch and watch semantics.

li (product): thanks — i'll review the UX section.

ana (arch) ana (arch): thanks all.
